name: Traditional Lashing (Rattan / Palm-fiber Tie)
description: Culms bound at crossings with rattan strips, palm fiber, or nylon cord. The oldest Filipino bamboo connection, used throughout the bahay kubo.
load_notes: Carries mainly compression and light shear; limited tension capacity; ties loosen as the culm shrinks on drying, so re-tightening or synthetic cord is common. Capacities are not standardized — for engineered work use tested connections per ISO 22156.
failure_mode: Tie loosening/slippage and local crushing at the contact point.
sources: ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Bamboo culms — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html
INBAR — International Bamboo and Rattan Organisation (structural use of bamboo): https://www.inbar.int/

name: Pin / Dowel Joint
description: A hardwood or bamboo dowel driven through drilled culms to lock members together, often combined with lashing.
load_notes: Resists shear across the joint better than lashing alone; drilling reduces the culm's net section and can initiate splitting, so hole placement and edge distance matter.
failure_mode: Longitudinal splitting of the culm at the drilled hole; dowel shear.
sources: ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html
Base Bahay — Manual for the design of bamboo structures to ISO 22156:2021: https://base-builds.com/manual-for-the-design-of-bamboo-structures-to-iso-221562021/

name: Bolted Joint
description: Through-bolts with washers clamp culms or connect them to steel plates. Common in modern engineered bamboo.
load_notes: Higher and more predictable capacity than ties, but bolt bearing can crush thin walls or split the culm without reinforcement — hence the mortar-plug variant below. Design per ISO 22156.
failure_mode: Wall crushing at the bolt hole; longitudinal splitting.
sources: ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html
Base Bahay — Manual for the design of bamboo structures to ISO 22156:2021: https://base-builds.com/manual-for-the-design-of-bamboo-structures-to-iso-221562021/

name: Bolted + Mortar-Plug Joint
description: The culm cavity at the connection is filled with cement mortar before bolting, so the bolt bears on a solid plug instead of the thin wall. This is the core connection of Base Bahay's Cement-Bamboo Frame Technology (CBFT).
load_notes: Substantially raises bolt-bearing capacity and reduces splitting; adds weight and requires curing. Field-proven at scale — 2,400+ CBFT houses built across the Philippines, Nepal, India and Sri Lanka have withstood typhoons and earthquakes.
failure_mode: Plug pull-out or culm splitting beyond the plug.
sources: Base Bahay Foundation — Cement Bamboo Frame Technology: https://base-builds.com/cement-bamboo-frame-technology/
Lateral Overturning Tests of Cement-Bamboo Frame Technology Panels (ISO 21581 Method II): https://www.hrpub.org/journals/article_info.php?aid=15621
ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html

name: Steel-Strap / Gusset Joint
description: Formed steel straps, clamps, or gusset plates wrap or bracket multiple culms at a node — used for trusses and heavier framing.
load_notes: Distributes load over a larger contact area than a single bolt; performance depends on strap tightness, node detailing, and corrosion protection of the steel.
failure_mode: Strap slippage, steel corrosion, or local culm crushing under the clamp.
sources: ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html
Base Bahay — Manual for the design of bamboo structures to ISO 22156:2021: https://base-builds.com/manual-for-the-design-of-bamboo-structures-to-iso-221562021/

name: Fish-Mouth (Saddle) Joint
description: The end of one culm is cut to a concave 'fish-mouth' profile so it seats snugly onto a perpendicular culm, then lashed or bolted.
load_notes: Improves bearing contact and alignment at right-angle connections; still relies on a tie or bolt to carry tension, since the cut itself only transfers compression/bearing.
failure_mode: Crushing at the saddle contact; failure of the tie or bolt under tension.
sources: ISO 22156:2021 — Bamboo structures — Structural design: https://www.iso.org/standard/73831.html
INBAR — International Bamboo and Rattan Organisation: https://www.inbar.int/
